transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is... some evenings after work, I end up eating way more than I meant to. 

It seems to happen especially when I've been really strict with myself all day. I'll get home and have dinner, but then I just kind of keep going. I'll have a bowl of cereal, some crackers, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and then sweets—just eating all of it within a couple of hours.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don't do that. I've never made myself throw up.
After these episodes, do you do anything to compensate for the eating, such as fasting, exercising excessively, or using laxatives?

Yeah, I do. I don't use laxatives or anything like that, but... well, the next day after one of those nights, I'll tell myself I'm making up for it. 

I usually do that by skipping breakfast and lunch. Or sometimes I'll go take an extra-long hike, or just push myself a lot harder at softball conditioning—even when I'm really tired, I just feel like I have to do it to balance things out.
In a typical week, how many times do you have an episode of eating this way followed by fasting or extra exercise?

Well, for the past few months, I'd say it happens most weeks. Usually, it's about one or two nights a week where I just eat far more than I planned. And then... yeah, the next day is when I try to make up for it by skipping meals or exercising longer.
How much do your body shape or weight affect how you judge yourself as a person?

Well, it affects me quite a bit, honestly. Like... if my waistband feels tight right before a client luncheon or a leadership meeting, I start feeling like I just look sloppy. And then I worry that people won't take me as seriously. It bothers me because, I mean, I know I've still been doing my job well, but I just get so hung up on how my clothes fit in those moments and it makes me doubt myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent binge-eating episodes with subjective loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory fasting and excessive exercise occurring approximately 1–2 times weekly for the past few months. Self-evaluation is substantially influenced by body shape and weight, supporting bulimia nervosa. No self-induced vomiting is required for the diagnosis.

confirmed_symptoms: Episodes of eating substantially more than intended within a couple of hours
Continues eating through multiple foods, including cereal, crackers, leftovers, and sweets
Reports difficulty stopping once the episode begins
Skips breakfast and lunch the day after binge-eating episodes
Engages in extra-long hikes or unusually intense softball conditioning to compensate
Compensatory behaviors occur after approximately 1–2 binge-eating episodes per week
Body shape and weight-related clothing fit substantially affect self-evaluation
Feels sloppy and doubts herself when her waistband feels tight
Worries that perceived appearance will affect how seriously others take her
